democratic.summary: Documents support clean-energy investment, resilient infrastructure, climate regulation, renewable incentives, and ending oil-and-gas subsidies, alongside broader rural, housing, manufacturing, trade, and worker-investment proposals.
democratic.caveat: This broad bucket also contains unrelated economic proposals and retrospective administration claims.

republican.summary: Documents support domestic energy supply and independence through markets, fossil fuels, nuclear power, and pipelines, while earlier texts also endorse renewables, efficiency, and climate-risk responses.
republican.caveat: Energy sources and climate framing vary across years; the bucket also includes trade and general growth claims.

dsa.summary: Documents support Green New Deal programs, rapid fossil-fuel phaseout, massive public investment, and public or social ownership of energy, transit, infrastructure, and major industry.
dsa.caveat: Fallback documents also include broad economic restructuring, organizational, and unrelated movement claims.

democratic_vs_republican.summary: Democratic documents emphasize clean public investment and renewable incentives; Republican documents emphasize market-led supply, pipelines, and fossil-energy expansion, despite earlier climate and renewable provisions.

democratic_vs_dsa.summary: Both support clean-energy transition; Democratic documents use regulation, incentives, and investment, while DSA documents call for fossil-fuel phaseout and public or social ownership.

republican_vs_dsa.summary: Republican documents favor market-led domestic production including fossil fuels and pipelines; DSA documents favor public ownership, massive public investment, and phasing out fossil fuels.
